## Abstract

This study provides a comprehensive econometric analysis of financial volatility dynamics and macroeconomic interdependencies across three distinct datasets.

First, using a single time series representing the log-prices of a financial asset, we investigate time-varying volatility to capture clustering and persistence in market risk.

Second, we analyze a database of three financial time series to examine the extent to which asset returns follow interconnected and time-varying volatility paths, assessing their dynamic co-movements.

Finally, the research explores the transmission of oil price shocks within a small open economy using a dataset of macroeconomic variables, including oil prices, inflation, and GDP growth. By estimating a Vector Autoregression (VAR) model, we calculate structural impulse response functions to discuss the propagation mechanism and the dynamic impact of energy shocks on the domestic economy.
